title: Edge must clear friction
claim: Positive expectancy must beat friction; psychology is not an edge.
support: Friction drag and expectancy are explicit.
mechanism: Gross edge must exceed costs.
assumptions: Repeated-trade sample exists.
failure_modes: Small edges vanish after fees/slippage.

title: Probability and payoff interact
claim: High win rate and high reward/risk are both valid only through expectancy interaction.
support: The text contrasts win-rate and payout profiles.
mechanism: Expectancy depends on both hit rate and payoff.
assumptions: Trade distribution is stable enough to summarize.
failure_modes: Optimizing one metric can damage the other.

title: Use clean consistent charts
claim: Charts should keep price primary and remain visually consistent.
support: Grimes favors clarity, consistency, and price-first charts.
mechanism: Stable presentation improves discretionary reading.
assumptions: Trader uses visual analysis.
failure_modes: Indicator clutter hides structure.

title: Avoid equilibrium regimes
claim: Equilibrium periods are close to random walk behavior and should be avoided.
support: Balanced markets are described as highly random.
mechanism: Only imbalance creates directional opportunity.
assumptions: Imbalance shows up in price often enough to exploit.
failure_modes: Flat regimes bait overtrading.

title: Split regime from trigger
claim: Inference: systematic research should separate regime qualification from entry timing.

source.section: Defining a Trading Edge; The Two Forces

support: Edge is framed as finding less-random spots, not predicting everywhere.
mechanism: Two-stage design limits signals in no-edge conditions.
assumptions: Regimes can be labeled without look-ahead.
failure_modes: Overfit filters can suppress real signal.

title: Accumulation hides in flat ranges
claim: Accumulation can look like a dull flat range; springs reveal buying only in context.
support: Accumulation is described as sideways action that masks smart-money buying.
mechanism: Large buyers work passively to avoid lifting price.
assumptions: Liquidity allows stealth accumulation.
failure_modes: Long lower shadows alone have no edge.

title: Accumulation breakouts are hard to time
claim: Buying the breakout above an accumulation range often executes at bad spots.
support: The book warns about noisy boundaries and false spikes.
mechanism: Range noise flushes weak traders before trend resolution.
assumptions: Trader acts before clear trend confirmation.
failure_modes: Repeated attempts pile up small losses.

title: Four-trade taxonomy
claim: Technical trades reduce to continuation, termination, holding, and failing.
support: Grimes presents four root trade types.
mechanism: Trade type should match context and management style.
assumptions: Categories are broad enough to absorb variants.
failure_modes: Using the wrong management model hurts results.

title: Impulse-retracement-impulse is fundamental
claim: Trend movement is fundamentally impulse, retracement, impulse across time frames.
support: The chapter defines the three-leg pattern and calls it fractal.
mechanism: Orders and crowd response create staggered movement.
assumptions: Liquidity is sufficient to express structure.
failure_modes: News shocks can distort the pattern.

title: Intact trends need quiet pullbacks
claim: An intact trend shows follow-through in each leg and lacks sharp countertrend momentum in pullbacks.
support: Probabilities favor the next pullback only when impulse legs stay consistent.
mechanism: Continuation requires persistent imbalance.
assumptions: Recent legs are comparable on the same frame.
failure_modes: Violent counter-moves can mean the trend is broken.

title: Do not buy after a climax
claim: Potential climax or exhaustion means trend traders should skip the next pullback.
support: The book ties blow-offs to exhaustion and warns trend traders off the next pullback.
mechanism: Extreme one-sided participation leaves the move vulnerable.
assumptions: The move is extreme relative to recent history.
failure_modes: Range breakouts can look climactic yet continue.

title: Momentum divergence weakens the next entry
claim: If price makes a new extreme without momentum confirmation, avoid the next pullback entry.
support: The chapter explicitly pairs confirmation highs with buyable pullbacks and divergence with avoidance.
mechanism: Weaker momentum suggests the push is tiring.
assumptions: Momentum is measured consistently.
failure_modes: Divergence may resolve through chop, not instant reversal.

title: Pullback depth is approximate
claim: Useful retracement depth is broad, roughly 25 to 75 percent, not a precise ratio.
support: Exact ratios are dismissed as too noisy.
mechanism: Approximate depth carries information; exact levels do not.
assumptions: Prior leg is meaningful rather than random.
failure_modes: Fixed retracement entries alone can force huge stops.

title: Good pullbacks are quieter and cleaner
claim: The best pullbacks show reduced activity and relatively symmetrical geometry.
support: Orderly pullbacks are contrasted with erratic ones.
mechanism: Healthy pullbacks are rest, not aggressive opposition.
assumptions: The parent trend is still valid.
failure_modes: Complex pullbacks can stop out simple entries.

title: Levels are only potential zones
claim: Support and resistance are potential zones, not exact lines or certainties.
support: Grimes repeatedly qualifies levels as potential and zone-like.
mechanism: Noise and overshoots are normal around real levels.
assumptions: Analysis is done at the hard right edge.
failure_modes: Exact-line thinking causes false precision.

title: Holding levels show price rejection
claim: A level that will hold normally shows immediate price rejection away from the zone.
support: The chapter calls sharp rejection the archetype of a holding level.
mechanism: Real opposing liquidity reveals itself as urgency away from the level.
assumptions: The zone is meaningful in context.
failure_modes: Slow drift into a level often precedes a break.

title: Repeated tests weaken a level
claim: After two tests traders should be suspicious; after three or more tests odds shift toward failure.
support: The book rejects the old idea that more tests strengthen the level.
mechanism: Each retest consumes liquidity and shows weaker rejection.
assumptions: Tests belong to the same structure.
failure_modes: Some messy levels still hold.

title: Test early versus late retests
claim: Hypothesis: first/second tests with rejection outperform third-plus tests of the same zone.
support: Derived from the book’s multiple-test and rejection logic.
mechanism: Fresh liquidity should be stronger early than late.
assumptions: A repeatable rule can count tests objectively.
failure_modes: Bad zone-clustering can corrupt the count.

title: Most naked breakouts fail
claim: Indiscriminate breakout entry is worn down by failed breaks, low liquidity, volatility, and costs.

source.section: Breakout Trade: Trading Range to Trend

support: The book says most breakouts fail and costs eat the account by a thousand cuts.
mechanism: Public breakout orders are easy to trap or fade.
assumptions: Entry is taken without meaningful context filters.
failure_modes: Slippage and spread widen the damage.

title: Compression improves breakout quality
claim: Higher lows into resistance or a tight range near the extreme of a larger range often precede better breakouts.
support: The chapter links shallower pullbacks and edge compression to stronger breakouts.
mechanism: Compression suggests urgency and pre-positioning.
assumptions: The range and edge are clearly defined.
failure_modes: Apparent compression can still fail without sponsorship.

title: Best breakout failures reverse fast
claim: A good breakout failure spends at most two or three bars beyond the level, then reverses back through it with force.

source.section: Breakout Trade: Trading Range to Trend

support: The book gives a concrete 2-3 bar rule of thumb for failure.
mechanism: Trapped breakout traders must exit urgently.
assumptions: A clean level and quick failed excursion exist.
failure_modes: Comfortable consolidation outside the level can still be healthy.

title: Trend endings usually advertise themselves
claim: Momentum divergence, very high volatility/climax, and many same-direction legs often precede trend failure.
support: The chapter says failed pullbacks are often preceded by divergence and late-leg extension.
mechanism: Old-trend pushes lose conviction before they die.
assumptions: The trend is mature enough for exhaustion clues to matter.
failure_modes: Rare news shocks can reverse with little warning.

title: Two opposite impulse moves often mean triangle
claim: A sharp move one way immediately followed by a sharp move the other way usually leads to difficult consolidation.
support: The book says this often produces a triangle-like structure best avoided.
mechanism: Violent opposing shocks reset price into balance.
assumptions: Both opposing moves are large relative to recent action.
failure_modes: Strong mean-reversion specialists may still trade it.

title: Failure test entry and stop are precise
claim: Enter after price pierces a clear level and closes back through it; stop goes beyond the extreme excursion.
support: The template defines both trigger and stop location clearly.
mechanism: The setup monetizes trapped breakout traders while defining risk.
assumptions: Market is extended or reversal-primed.
failure_modes: Gap risk can jump the stop.

title: Good failure tests should work quickly
claim: A valid failure test should move away from the level within about one to three bars; lingering near the level is bad.
support: The book says consolidation near the level usually means trouble.
mechanism: Real rejection should produce immediate follow-through.
assumptions: Bars are counted on the trading frame.
failure_modes: Slow drift often precedes continuation and stop-out.

title: Pullbacks are robust only in real trends
claim: Pullbacks are robust discretionary trades only when the market is genuinely trending and the pullback is relatively quiet.

source.section: Pullback, Buying Support or Shorting Resistance

support: The setup requires a momentum setup leg and reduced-activity retracement.
mechanism: Trend traders use impulse-retracement-impulse to enter at better prices.
assumptions: No major contradictory conditions are present.
failure_modes: Nontrending markets turn pullbacks into chop.

title: Avoid many support tests inside a pullback
claim: Buying after three or more support tests within one pullback is lower quality and often points to failure.

source.section: Pullback, Buying Support or Shorting Resistance

support: The chapter explicitly warns against multiple tests in pullbacks.
mechanism: Successive tests show weak rejection and fewer willing buyers.
assumptions: Tests belong to one coherent pullback.
failure_modes: Messy pullbacks occasionally still resolve higher.

title: Nest a lower-TF breakout inside a higher-TF pullback
claim: Hypothesis: a lower-timeframe breakout aligned with a qualified higher-timeframe pullback outperforms a standalone lower-timeframe breakout.

source.section: Pullback, Entering Lower Time Frame Breakout

support: The book says the lower-timeframe breakout is ordinary alone but stronger inside the higher-timeframe pullback.
mechanism: Context supplies direction while the lower frame supplies timing.
assumptions: Time frames are properly nested.
failure_modes: Gap opens and over-tight stops can erase the edge.

title: No moving average is magical
claim: Tests do not show a special moving average or an edge in average touches by themselves.

source.section: The Moving Average - The Still Center

support: The book rejects lore about a privileged moving average.
mechanism: A moving average is mainly a summary or reference tool.
assumptions: Edge is sought in the average itself.
failure_modes: Mechanical MA-touch rules can mistake lore for evidence.

title: Flat around the average means move on
claim: Markets chopping around an intermediate average are usually equilibrium and are best skipped.
support: The chapter says markets near the average usually lack persistent imbalance.
mechanism: Repeated crossing implies no stable directional conviction.
assumptions: The average tracks the relevant consensus zone.
failure_modes: Strong moves can still begin from flat zones.

title: Fade bands only at real extension
claim: Band fades make sense only when price is truly extended; band slides are usually stand-aside conditions.
support: The book warns that blind band fading can create staggering losses and that band slides are hard to trade.
mechanism: Bands proxy overextension, but persistent band-riding signals exceptional imbalance.
assumptions: Band calibration is sensible for the market.
failure_modes: Amateurs fade every touch and get trapped.

title: Neighboring time frames filter and time trades
claim: Use multiple time frames to identify dominant structure, filter lower-quality trades, and improve timing; do not assume the higher frame always dominates.
support: The chapter explicitly rejects the naive “higher time frame always matters most” idea.
mechanism: Context and timing can come from different but related structures.
assumptions: Frames are analyzed without look-ahead.
failure_modes: Overcomplicated multi-frame logic can confuse weak chart readers.

title: Exits must respect signal horizon
claim: Stop and target choices must fit the actual horizon of the setup; distant targets can destroy a short-lived edge.
support: The opening example says a short-horizon signal cannot simply be forced into large profits.
mechanism: When a signal decays quickly, far targets mostly harvest noise.
assumptions: Signal horizon can be estimated from research or repetition.
failure_modes: Preference-based target setting can kill a valid edge.

title: Use volatility or structure stops
claim: Fixed-percent stops are crude across markets; volatility-aware or structure-aware stops are more intelligent.
support: The chapter contrasts identical percent stops in low- and high-volatility stocks.
mechanism: Stop distance should reflect local noise and market geometry.
assumptions: ATR or pivots are measured sensibly.
failure_modes: Stops inside noise get hit without invalidating the trade.

title: Never average in without a hard risk cap
claim: Scaling into a losing trade is dangerous unless total dollar risk and the final stop are tracked continuously.
support: The chapter calls this behavior unacceptable and dangerous.
mechanism: Averaging in raises size and emotional commitment while price is moving the wrong way.
assumptions: Trader enters in pieces.
failure_modes: Loss can quietly exceed plan and become catastrophic.

title: Know the exit before the entry
claim: Define the wrong-point before entry and keep the initial stop outside noise, usually not inside one average bar range.
support: Grimes calls this perhaps the single most important rule in discretionary trading.
mechanism: Predefined invalidation converts uncertainty into measurable risk.
assumptions: Average bar range is a useful noise proxy.
failure_modes: Noise-level stops damage edge via avoidable stop-outs.

title: Kelly-style sizing is assumption-fragile
claim: Optimized Kelly/optimal-f sizing can fail badly when independence or stationarity assumptions break.
support: The chapter warns about serial dependence and larger future losses than history suggested.
mechanism: Aggressive optimization magnifies model error in clustered or fat-tail outcomes.
assumptions: Trader uses optimized sizing instead of a robust cap.
failure_modes: Regime shifts can turn sizing error into ruin.

title: Fixed-fraction sizing is for survival first
claim: Simple fixed-fraction sizing aims to control downside, with under 1% conservative and 3%+ aggressive.
support: The design goals focus on limiting outsized losses, streaks, and correlation risk.
mechanism: Sizing as a fraction of equity scales risk naturally and protects survival.
assumptions: Per-trade risk from entry to stop can be computed.
failure_modes: Correlated trades or gaps can still exceed plan.

title: Psychology cannot replace edge
claim: Meditation, positive thinking, and visualization cannot substitute for a real trading edge.
support: The psychology chapter explicitly repeats this warning.
mechanism: Mindset helps execution; it does not create expectancy.
assumptions: Trading style needs discretionary execution quality.
failure_modes: Negative expectancy can be misdiagnosed as a mindset issue.

title: Use large samples because reinforcement is noisy
claim: Markets randomly reward bad behavior and punish good behavior in small samples, so rule changes require many trades.
support: Grimes says learn from 20-30 trades, not one, and change rules from 50, not five.
mechanism: Large samples reduce random reinforcement error.
assumptions: The setup class is stable enough to pool.
failure_modes: Tiny samples breed superstition and bad heuristics.

title: Trader development is multi-year
claim: Early trader development is expected to lose, then lose more slowly, then merely cover costs before competence.
support: The chapter lays out a multi-year progression from pretrader to proficient trader.
mechanism: Skill is apprenticeship-like and built through review and exposure.
assumptions: Development is self-directed and discretionary.
failure_modes: Unrealistic time-to-profit expectations force bad risk-taking.

title: Journals and categorized P&L are control tools
claim: Solid journals, daily game plans, and P&L categorized by setup and initial risk are essential for finding what really works.
support: The book says novice-to-expert progress is virtually impossible without a solid journal and setup-tagged records.
mechanism: Good records turn subjective trading into analyzable samples.
assumptions: Records are kept consistently and not recoded after the fact.
failure_modes: Sparse or revised records hide drift and bias analysis.
